scope_lock.slice: authenticated bundle, capture setup, provisioning apply, and database-backed readback propagation
scope_lock.objective: Make runtime-asset closure authority mandatory and immutable across the current bundle-authenticated capture/readback lifecycle, including all composite commands, before any nav, output, provisioning, database, or worldserver side effect.
required_behavior: Expose one canonical helper that renders and validates the complete closure argument tuple from explicit verified roots, bundle/config identity, scenario map ID, manifest, audit authority, inventory authority, and extraction receipt binding. Never derive a root from cwd.
Make capture setup and database-backed provisioning readback reject total omission and partial closure authority before their first downstream side effect. Omission must never mean approval.

Have bundle creation derive the exact tuple from already verified source, DVC workspace, sealed bundle, config, and scenario identities, then include it in launch_argv before the bundle manifest is hashed and atomically sealed.

Have bundle verification require the exact closure tuple in launch_argv and reject omission, reordering that changes command identity, root substitution, map substitution, stale manifest/audit/inventory authority, and bundle/config path mismatch.

Have composite plan realization carry one identical closure authority into provisioning_apply, shard_readback, and the bundle-authenticated capture command; bind it in plan_sha256 and verify it immediately before each command executes.
The provisioning_apply invocation of run_live_bot_validation must contain the complete tuple even though the generic live entrypoint's total-omission rejection is deferred to the next work unit.
Preserve profile dialect behavior and keep map/scenario selection in the owning bundle/route module, not in the generic verifier.

Update the shard-architecture skill because optional-gate compatibility was a repeated wrong assumption: runtime asset omission is never approval on a side-effecting path, and generated commands must bind the full authority. Do not add canary-specific universal guidance.
deterministic_fixtures: Capture setup and readback with no tuple or a partial tuple reject before nav probing, contract materialization, DB URL resolution, output creation, or launch.
expected_launch_argv and both bundle dialects contain the exact canonical tuple, and bundle verification rejects any missing or mutated member.
Composite realization gives provisioning_apply, shard_readback, and capture the same closure identity; omission or mutation invalidates the plan before subprocess execution.
Existing capture/readback fixtures use an explicit valid fixture authority or mock only the completed verifier result, never an omission exemption.

explicitly_deferred.safety: No hydration, database operation, build, server, or live run is authorized until this and the next propagation slice both pass fresh review.

forbidden_changes: No edits outside the exact twelve owned paths.
No generic live/session caller edits in this slice.
No weakening of RAC-002 through RAC-005 authority checks.

No asset copy/hydration, extraction receipt creation, DVC operation, database access, provisioning execution, build, capture, worldserver start, live run, gameplay, encounter, class, role, roster, or movement change.
acceptance_conditions: Every normal authenticated bundle capture, provisioning-apply, and shard-readback command carries one exact closure tuple and total omission fails closed at capture/readback entrypoints.
Generated command, bundle, and composite plan hashes bind the closure authority and deterministic mutation tests pass.
Exactly the twelve owned paths change in one commit, the skill validates, and the worktree is clean.
The generic live/session slice remains explicitly unresolved and no checklist acceptance or live authorization claim is made.

terminal_conditions.success: Return one committed bundle-path propagation correction and route immediately to the generic live/session propagation slice.
terminal_conditions.failed_verification: Stop with the earliest typed failure and do not broaden ownership.
terminal_conditions.out_of_scope: Report generic live/session, hydration, provenance creation, DVC, build, or live needs without acting on them.

next_action: Dispatch one Sol high raid-shard-architecture implementer, then authorize the generic live/session propagation slice before fresh review.
